title: Calcium intake and risk of fracture: systematic review
authors: Bolland MJ, Leung W, Tai V, Bastin S, Gamble GD, Grey A, et al.
population: Adults older than 50 years; searches to September 2014
funder: Health Research Council of New Zealand. The authors are independent of the HRC, which had no role in study design, data collection, analysis, interpretation, writing or the decision to submit.
authorConflicts: IRR has received research grants or honorariums from Merck, Amgen, Lilly and Novartis.
result: Two randomised trials of dietary calcium sources reported fractures (262 participants); in the milk-powder trial (100 versus 100 women) there was 1 fracture versus 3 (RR 0.33, 95% CI 0.04 to 3.2). In cohort studies, 25 of 28 associations of milk intake and 11 of 13 of dairy intake with fracture were null. Calcium supplements: total fracture RR 0.89 (0.81 to 0.96; 20 trials), hip fracture 0.95 (0.76 to 1.18); no effect at any site in the 4 trials at lowest risk of bias.
